statement.p: Find the differential of f(x,y) = \sqrt{x^{2}+y^{3}} at the point (3,1).
Then use the differential to estimate f(2.92,0.9).

static.solution:
f_x(x,y) = and f_y(x,y) =, f_x(3,1) = and f_y(3,1) =.
Thus the differential at the point (3,1) is df = df(3,1) = f_x(3,1)\,dx + f_y(3,1)\,dy = 0.948683dx+0.474342dy.
Using the differential at the point (3,1), we can estimate f(2.92,0.9). Since \Delta f \approx f_x(3,1)\Delta x + f_y(3,1)\Delta y, where \Delta f = f(2.92,0.9) - f(3,1) and \Delta x = 2.92 - 3 and \Delta y = 0.9 - 1, we have f(2.92,0.9) \approx f(3,1) + f_x(3,1)(2.92-3) + f_y(3,1)(0.9-1) \approx 3.16228 + \,(-0.08) + (-0.1) = 3.03895.
